findings.text: Polling interface provides a cookie representing current grace period progress and a starter that ensures progress. Obtaining the cookie orders prior protected updates before the snapshot. Starting a poll reuses the cookie mechanism under interrupt disabled node protection and wakes the grace period thread only when the starter indicates need.

Blocking expedited wait is forbidden inside read side sections and degrades gracefully. A configuration where blocking itself implies a quiescent state completes vacuously with a sequence advance. When expedited handling is administratively disabled the request falls back to the normal wait. Otherwise the caller snapshots, coalesces with concurrent requesters, queues or directly executes selection, sleeps until its snapshot is marked complete, then releases the global expedited guard.

Normal deferred requests use a best effort latch to choose between accelerated and fallback handling. The shared counter is increased before the request becomes visible to consumers. Only the updater observing the exact threshold attempts to set the flag, so at most one context contends on the atomic update. Concurrent set and clear may lose the indication, which remains safe because it affects only path selection.

Expedited progress is tracked by a monotonic sequence with snapshot, active, and completion states plus a parallel polled snapshot. Snapshots enforce that caller stores are visible to peers before the value is read. Completion checks pair with the terminating barrier to order both earlier and later updates. Starting and ending advance both trackers together, and consecutive periods are serialized by a barrier after termination.

Concurrent expedited requests coalesce through per node desired values and a single global guard. An uncontended attempt succeeds when both local and root desires are older and the guard is free. Otherwise the desired value propagates toward the root, with followers sleeping on the node queue when their snapshot is already covered. The guard holder rechecks coverage before announcing a new period, allowing late arrivals to share work.

An expedited period moves through tree preparation, processor selection, blocking wait, and ordered wakeup. Preparation refreshes membership for newly arrived processors and captures any blocked readers on leaves. Selection runs per leaf either inline or on helpers with a completion barrier. After the blocking wait finishes, completion is published under a dedicated wake guard, outstanding desires are advanced to the finished value, all node queues are awakened, and leaf cleanup for offloaded handling runs.

Leaf selection treats the local processor and processors absent from the next initialization set as already quiescent. Other processors are classified by an acquire watching snapshot, with idle ones excused immediately and the snapshot retained otherwise. Before signaling, the retained snapshot is rechecked for a transition into non watching state and for migration onto the current processor. Remaining processors receive a wakeup request, with transient hotplug failures retried after a short idle delay and genuinely offline processors reported together under node protection.

Tree mutation and inspection occur under interrupt disabled raw node protection, including mask updates, task list capture, hotplug propagation, selection reporting, completion tests, and stall dumps. Desired sequence publication uses a small separate spin guard per node to coordinate followers. A global mutex serializes at most one active expedited period, while a distinct wake mutex serializes publication of completion against concurrent wakeups. Polling start disables interrupts locally while holding only its leaf node guard.

Expedited entry warns when invoked while holding read side markers and must not be used from atomic or non sleepable contexts because it sleeps on node and global queues. The wait loop can emit extended stall diagnostics, invoke notifiers, and trigger a panic on persistent absence of progress, with task detail output potentially voluminous while holding node protection. Hotplug races during signaling require retry logic to avoid misclassifying a present processor as offline.

Whether blocked readers can delay an expedited period depends on build configuration. One variant reports presence by testing emptiness of the node blocked list, the other reports absence unconditionally. Tree preparation consults this predicate on leaves only and, when true, anchors the expedited task pointer at the current tail of that list.

Early boot and scheduler inactive conditions execute expedited selection inline in the requester context. Once scheduling and dedicated workers are available, selection and period work are queued to those workers, with leaf helpers flushed before proceeding. Parallel helpers use a distinct worker from the initiator to avoid self flush deadlock, and the final leaf in order is handled inline.
Leaf membership encodes each processor as a single bit whose position equals its identifier minus the low identifier of the owning group.

Hotplug refresh is skipped when the cached processor count matches the current count. Otherwise each leaf adopts its pending initialization set and only leaves transitioning from empty propagate a group bit upward. Propagation stops at the first ancestor that already had a non empty set, limiting upward churn.

The blocking wait first attempts a bounded sleep, and on full dynticks systems may arm tick dependencies for outstanding processors before a second bounded attempt. Thereafter it loops indefinitely, skipping dumps while stalls are suppressed and otherwise collecting the set of lagging processors and tasks, emitting state, backing off the next check interval, and invoking the panic policy.
